message:
## Vulnerability Digest

**Scan window:** 2026-09-11 05:10 IST to 2026-09-12 05:10 IST (2026-09-10 23:40 UTC to 2026-09-11 23:40 UTC)

This primary product scan read, normalized, and deduplicated only `Products.txt` and `List_of_SIA_Completed.txt`. One high-priority exploitation development directly matched the monitored SonicWall SMA 8200V. One newly published GNU C Library issue is retained as a possible Ubuntu match pending Ubuntu-specific confirmation.

### Findings

**Finding 1 — Active exploitation reporting for SonicWall SMA1000 (CVE-2026-15409)**

- **Affected product/component:** SonicWall SMA1000 Series, including the monitored SMA 8200V
- **Severity:** Critical, CVSS 10.0 (SonicWall)
- **Description:** New reporting on September 11 covered Hunt.io research linking a campaign, with moderate confidence, to mass exploitation of the unauthenticated SSRF flaw. The research says compromised appliances were used to extract LDAP configuration and credentials and pivot toward internal Active Directory environments.
- **Relevance:** `SonicWall SMA 8200V` is explicitly listed in the assigned product inventory, and SonicWall's advisory identifies SMA1000 Series appliances as affected.
- **Sources:** [Hunt.io research](https://hunt.io/blog/sonicwall-sma1000-uk-council-attack), [SonicWall advisory](https://psirt.global.sonicwall.com/vuln-detail/SNWLID-2026-0008), [September 11 reporting](https://securityaffairs.com/198864/hacking/uk-council-attack-linked-to-mass-exploitation-of-sonicwall-flaw.html)

### Possible matches needing review

**GNU C Library nscd stack overflow (CVE-2026-89092)**

- **Potentially affected product/component:** Ubuntu systems using glibc's `nscd`
- **Severity:** Medium, CVSS 3.1 score 4.2
- **Description:** A malicious DNS server can return an oversized response that causes a stack overflow and crash in `nscd`, degrading name-resolution performance. Exploitation requires `nscd` to be enabled and the system to use an untrusted or compromised DNS server.
- **Why uncertain:** glibc is a core Ubuntu component, but no in-window Canonical notice was found confirming which Ubuntu releases or packages are affected by this newly published CVE.
- **Sources:** [GNU glibc advisory](https://sourceware.org/git/?p=glibc.git;a=blob_plain;f=advisories/GLIBC-SA-2026-0016), [NVD record](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-89092)

### MongoDB ecosystem sweep

A dedicated sweep checked MongoDB Server Community and Enterprise, `mongod`, `mongos`, Atlas and Atlas services, Ops Manager, Cloud Manager, Compass, `mongosh`, Database Tools, Kubernetes Operator, drivers, connectors, BI Connector, Charts, Realm/App Services, official integrations, MongoDB-owned advisories whose titles may omit “MongoDB,” GitHub advisories, NVD/CVE records, and CISA-oriented sources.

No credible MongoDB-related vulnerability was newly reported or materially updated inside this scan window. MongoDB's newest authoritative security batch was dated September 8, 2026. A MongoDB Go Driver 2.9.1 release addressing CVE-2026-88031 was announced at 20:49 UTC on September 10, about three hours before this run's cutoff, and was excluded as stale. [MongoDB Alerts](https://www.mongodb.com/resources/products/alerts), [MongoDB Go Driver release](https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/mongodb-go-driver-2-9-1-released/343343)

### Closing

Immediate review is recommended for any deployed SonicWall SMA 8200V appliance because the newly reported campaign describes credential theft and internal-network pivoting from exploited appliances. Review Ubuntu exposure to CVE-2026-89092 once Canonical publishes package-specific status. No other credible in-window findings were retained for the monitored products.
